checks.reason: OPS-01 objectives measured on the live sandbox run: control-plane availability 6414/6414 probes non-5xx (100.00%, 95% lower bound 99.95% vs target 99.90%: demonstrated) from runner-local probes of the API readiness route every 100 ms, paused only for the deliberate database loss (13 s, measured as RTO); API latency p50 13 ms, p95 27 ms, p99 104 ms, 100.00% within 500 ms (lower bound 99.95% vs 95.00%: demonstrated); capacity 29.9 req/s served of 30 offered for 60 s, p95 252 ms, errors 0.00% (targets >= 25 req/s, p95 <= 500 ms, errors <= 0.50%: within_target); RPO 204.052 s of 900 and RTO 20.733 s of 14400 (one restore observation each: within_target, within_target); target file 2026-10-13.1 (approved_targets), measurement label provisional; not evaluated: managed_runtime_availability, dispatch_latency, workflow_completion, scheduler_health

OPS-04 restore proven on AWS: a deploy waiting for its approval was captured in the backup and approved and applied after it; the stores were lost from the control-plane database and restored into it at recovery epoch 1; the restored proposal was fenced (an approval was refused: journey:browser-human-approval), did not execute on its own for 120 s, and came back only through a recovery resume (a stale binding was refused) and a fresh approval; applying it again left AWS unchanged (2 buckets, 16 recorded resources). Measured RPO 204.1 s (target 900) and RTO 20.7 s (target 14400)
